author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty
summary: Both veterinarian list surfaces — the directory page and the machine-readable list — accept an optional specialty selector that narrows the list to veterinarians holding that specialty, matched on the whole name and case-insensitively. A blank selector behaves as absent, an unmatched specialty yields an empty list successfully, and the machine-readable list becomes a supported surface.
acceptance_criteria: given a specialty that some veterinarians hold, when the directory page is narrowed to it, then only those veterinarians are listed a page at a time
given a specialty that some veterinarians hold, when the machine-readable list is narrowed to it, then it returns only those veterinarians
given a specialty name differing from a held specialty only by letter case, when either surface is narrowed to it, then it matches; a value that is only a prefix of a specialty name matches nothing
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either surface is narrowed to it, then the request succeeds and the veterinarian list is empty
given an empty or whitespace-only specialty, when either surface is requested, then the result is identical to requesting it with no specialty
given no specialty, when either surface is requested, then it behaves exactly as before this requirement
non_goals: Free-text veterinarian search — NG-9 keeps typed-name search to owners only
Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application — NG-2
notes: The new filtering behavior on both surfaces must be covered with tests (scope, not an acceptance criterion about the suite). The machine-readable /vets endpoint is reinstated as a supported surface under this fresh id; the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused — support follows a newly requested capability, not a reversal of the 2026-07-31 finding. NG-9 narrowed 2026-08-07 to admit filtering a directory by an attribute it already displays. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records in the log.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Adds a specialty filter to both vet surfaces by reusing the established owner-search pattern: a Spring Data derived query with paging (OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith) plus a thin controller branch on the normalized parameter (OwnerController.processFindForm). No new module, pattern, or type. VetController stays a thin Web-controller adapter; the filter lives in VetRepository, not the controller. Durable memory corrected in docs/system-design.md: the stale Known-Defects row framing /vets as 'pending removal, serving no requirement' is removed, and the Vets/VetRepository/VetController Contracts rows now cite REQ-VET-003 to reflect the reinstated machine-readable surface.
integration_points: VetController.showVetList gains an optional specialty @RequestParam; branches to the filtered repository method when the value is present, to the existing findAll(Pageable) when blank/absent
VetController.showResourcesVetList gains the same optional specialty @RequestParam; branches to an unpaged filtered method when present, to the existing findAll() when blank/absent
VetRepository gains two derived query methods traversing the Vet->specialties->name association: one returning Page<Vet> for the HTML surface, one returning Collection<Vet> for the JSON surface
vetList.html pagination links must carry the active specialty parameter so page N of a filtered list stays filtered

patterns.description: derived query + Pageable -> Page precedent; mirror it as a whole-name case-insensitive match (e.g. findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase) rather than StartingWith, so a prefix matches nothing
parameter normalization precedent: strip surrounding whitespace and treat null/blank as absent. Reuse the null/blank+strip rule, but NOT the empty-string-to-query trick

risks.risk: Copying OwnerController's empty-string-signifies-broadest-search trick would break blank handling: a whole-name equality match on "" matches no specialty and would return an empty list for blank input, failing blankSpecialtyReturnsFullVetList
risks.mitigation: After strip, branch blank/null explicitly to the unfiltered findAll path; only pass a non-blank, stripped value to the filtered query

risks.risk: Case-insensitivity done at the column/collation level would reproduce the PostgreSQL case-sensitivity defect that afflicts owner search (Known Defects), since specialty matching must hold across all three vendors
risks.mitigation: Match case-insensitively at query time via the derived-query IgnoreCase keyword (UPPER() in the generated JPQL), independent of column collation

risks.risk: A join across the specialties association can yield duplicate Vet rows
risks.mitigation: Use Distinct in the derived query so each matching veterinarian appears once

risks.risk: The submitted specialty echoed back into the page (e.g. to preserve the filter in pagination links) is untrusted input crossing into rendered HTML
risks.mitigation: Rely on Thymeleaf's default output escaping; do not disable it. The value reaches persistence only through the parameterized derived query, so no SQL-injection surface is introduced

notes: Verdict minor: existing owner-search pattern extended by a parameter and two repository extension points; small docs/system-design.md edit only. No ADR: the filter follows the in-force derived-query + Web-controller patterns with no trade-off to record, and the /vets reinstatement is a product decision already recorded in docs/prd.md (Superseded, updated 2026-08-07). No new business rule enters the controller: pagination stays at the DB layer via the paged derived query, so the Web-controller 'no business rule' bar is respected. Caching: the existing methods carry @Cacheable("vets"); adding the same annotation to the filtered methods is consistent and safe given vet data has no write path (Open Question 5 on eviction is unchanged), but correctness does not depend on it. If a visible specialty filter control is added to vetList.html, its label needs message-bundle keys in every locale (REQ-LANG-002); the behavioral requirement is satisfiable via the query parameter alone. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log.

approved_aspects: Reflected XSS mitigated: the untrusted specialty parameter reaches HTML only via Thymeleaf's URL-expression @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes query-parameter values; no th:utext or unescaped sink introduced (design-block XSS risk heeded)

/vets reinstatement exposes no new data: the machine-readable surface returns the same veterinarian and specialty fields already public on the HTML directory, and the app carries no auth boundary by design
normalizeSpecialty null/blank/whitespace handling keeps blank input off the query path without introducing an injection or logic-bypass surface
No hardcoded secrets in the diff; no build.gradle or dependency change, so no new supply-chain surface (framework versions unchanged)

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: All 7 new test methods fail the project BDD naming school (`the{Subject}Should{Outcome}`), which applies to tests written from 2026-07-31 onward. Current names are descriptive but use a present-tense or verb-phrase form rather than the required school: `filterVetListHtmlBySpecialty`, `filterVetResourcesBySpecialty`, `blankSpecialtyReturnsFullVetList`, `unmatchedSpecialtyReturnsEmptyVetList`, `noSpecialtyReturnsFullVetList`, `specialtyMatchIsCaseInsensitiveWholeName`, `prefixSpecialtyMatchesNoVet`. A name that survives renaming the production method is a behavior name; these do not.

AC5 coverage gap on the JSON surface. The `blankSpecialtyReturnsFullVetList` test only exercises `/vets.html` with a blank specialty. The JSON surface (`/vets?specialty=+`) is not tested. If `showResourcesVetList` lost its `normalizeSpecialty` call, the blank string would be passed directly to the filtered repository query, returning an empty list instead of the full list — and no test in the suite would fail. Both surfaces are declared in the acceptance criterion: 'given an empty or whitespace-only specialty, when either surface is requested, then the result is identical to requesting it with no specialty.'
findings.fix: Add a test (or extend `blankSpecialtyReturnsFullVetList`) that issues GET /vets with a blank specialty parameter and asserts HTTP 200 with both vets present in the JSON response and that `findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(anyString())` is never called.

findings.description: AC4 coverage gap on the HTML surface. The `unmatchedSpecialtyReturnsEmptyVetList` test only exercises the JSON surface (`/vets?specialty=cardiology`). The HTML surface (`/vets.html?specialty=cardiology`) with an unmatched specialty returning HTTP 200 with an empty paginated list is not tested. If the HTML branch crashed on an empty Page or incorrectly redirected, the suite would not catch it.
findings.fix: Add a controller test that issues GET /vets.html?specialty=cardiology, stubs `findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(eq("cardiology"), any(Pageable.class))` to return an empty Page, and asserts HTTP 200 and view name `vets/vetList`.

approved_aspects: Integration tests (`specialtyMatchIsCaseInsensitiveWholeName`, `prefixSpecialtyMatchesNoVet`) test query semantics against the real H2 database using actual seed data (Helen Leary + Henry Stevens hold 'radiology'); this is the correct level for verifying the IgnoreCase derived-query behavior and the whole-name vs prefix distinction
`filterVetListHtmlBySpecialty` verifies that pagination links carry the specialty parameter (`containsString("specialty=radiology")`), covering the vetList.html template change directly
Verify-never idiom correctly asserts that the filtered and unfiltered repository paths are mutually exclusive

Factory methods `james()`, `helen()`, `linda()`, `rafael()` properly encapsulate Vet construction in the controller test, following the brief's factory-method rule for tests written from 2026-07-31 onward
Coverage: vet package 100% line coverage; overall project 94.4% — well above the 80% target
AssertJ fluent assertions used throughout all new integration tests; MockMvc result matchers used correctly in controller tests; no JUnit `assertEquals` in new code

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Both new test methods declare a local variable named `vets` that shadows the field `this.vets` (the VetRepository). A reader scanning the assertion `assertThat(vets)` must trace back to line 218 or 226 to verify that `vets` is the result collection, not the repository. The field already occupies the name in this scope; a different local name removes the ambiguity. Class sweep: the pre-existing `shouldFindVets` at line 208 carries the same pattern but is outside the diff — the new tests copy it. Fix the new instances; the pre-existing one is a separate concern.
findings.fix: Rename the local variable in both new methods to `matchedVets` (or `result`): `Collection<Vet> matchedVets = this.vets.findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(...)`. Update the `assertThat(...)` call on the following line accordingly.

findings.description: The literal `6` passed as the third argument to `new PageImpl<>(Lists.newArrayList(helen()), PageRequest.of(0, 5), 6)` is a mystery literal. Its role — to make total elements exceed the page size (5) so the pagination controls render, letting the test assert that the specialty parameter appears in their URLs — requires mental arithmetic to decode. The testing principles prohibit mystery literals.
findings.fix: Extract a named constant at the top of the test class, e.g. `private static final int TOTAL_RESULTS_SPANNING_TWO_PAGES = 6;`, and reference it in the PageImpl constructor. Alternatively, add an inline comment: `// 6 > page-size (5): ensures pagination controls render`.

approved_aspects: Derived query name `findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase` is precise and mirrors the IgnoreCase + Distinct pattern the design-block prescribed
`normalizeSpecialty` private helper is documented with Javadoc and correctly short-circuits null and blank before reaching the repository
Thymeleaf `@{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})}` threads the filter through pagination links; null specialty is implicitly omitted by the URL builder, preserving the unfiltered URL shape
checkFormat passes clean: no formatting issues in the diff
@Cacheable on the two new filtered methods is consistent with the existing cached overloads and uses the same cache region
Four-phase Arrange/Act/Assert structure is properly separated with blank lines in every new test method
Factory methods `linda()` and `rafael()` follow the existing `james()` and `helen()` object-construction pattern already established in the class
